content.comment_body: Is there a way to create a one-shot function to prevent delays in the circuit from being reset? In the simulation, every time I press the input button twice, the set delay restarts. Is there a key function or method that can protect a 17-second timing sequence, for example, where after 2 seconds on and 15 seconds off, pushing the button again during this interval doesn't reset the timing?

Take a look at this solution. After pressing the push button for 2 seconds, Q1 becomes active and can't be triggered again for the next 15 seconds. A latching relay blocks the input to the timer until the timer completes its cycle.
Let me know if you find this helpful.

analysis.insight_summary: The user wanted a way to implement a single-shot function to prevent a timer from restarting within a 17-second interval. There was initial uncertainty about how to stop repeated inputs from interfering with the delay. Another participant suggested using a latching relay to lock out further input during the timer period, which resolved the concern and was confirmed to work as intended.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects an easy solution for a one-shot feature that ignores further button presses while the timer is running, making sure the set timing interval is not interrupted or reset by repeated inputs.
